item.title: Kenneth Okonkwo tackles Tinubu over Aso Rock water outage
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab A supporter of former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, Kenneth Okonkwo, has criticised President Bola Tinubu over his reported revelation that water supply was interrupted at the Presidential Villa, questioning how the president could address Nigerians’ needs when basic amenities were not consistently available at his residence. Okonkwo made the remarks in a post on his X account on Monday, where he described Tinubu’s comment about the water interruption at Aso Rock as evidence of what he considered the failure of the president’s administration. He argued that the inability to guarantee steady electricity and water supply at the seat of government raised questions about the administration’s capacity to provide the same necessities for Nigerians. “Without electricity, there is no industrialisation. Without water, there is no life,” he wrote. “If Tinubu could not give himself light and life, are you expecting him to give you what he doesn’t have?” Okonkwo asked. He also linked the development to the 2027 presidential election, warning Nigerians against voting for the All Progressives Congress and Tinubu. “Anyone voting for APC and Tinubu in 2027 is voting for darkness”, he said. Okonkwo subsequently called on Nigerians to support former Vice President Atiku Abubakar in the 2027 election, presenting him as an alternative capable of addressing the country’s electricity and water challenges. “An opportunity to rescue Nigeria has come”, he concluded. The NCDC continues routine COVID-19 surveillance and has reported sporadic confirmed cases during 2026. Because genomic sequencing in Africa is limited, absence of reports should not be taken as absence of the variant,” the statement noted. Among recommended preventive steps for all Nigerians, the Academy noted: “Stay home when unwell. Anyone with fever, cough, sore throat or flu-like illness should avoid work, school, church/mosque and social gatherings until well. Get tested. Use a COVID-19 rapid antigen test or visit a health facility if you have respiratory symptoms, especially if you are high-risk or care for high-risk people.” Further, the advisory urged: “Wear a well-fitting face mask in crowded indoor places, on public transport, in hospitals and clinics, when you have symptoms, and when visiting elderly or sick relatives. Wash hands frequently with soap and running water, or use an alcohol-based sanitiser, cover coughs and sneezes with a tissue or the bend of the elbow, and dispose of tissues safely. “Open windows and doors; hold events outdoors or in well-ventilated halls where possible. The Academy said available evidence did not justify travel bans and said its message to Nigerians is not to panic, but be vigilant, particularly in the coming festive season of travel, homecomings and large gatherings. It urged Nigerians experiencing fever, cough, sore throat or other flu-like symptoms to stay away from workplaces, schools, religious gatherings and social events until they recover. “Extra care is advised for people aged 60 and above; people with diabetes, hypertension, heart, lung or kidney disease, sickle cell disease, cancer, HIV or other immunosuppression; pregnant women; and people with obesity. The Academy cautioned people in these groups to keep their underlying conditions under control, maintain adequate supplies of prescribed medicines and seek medical attention early if symptoms develop, noting that early medical assessment was important because antiviral treatment, where indicated, works best when started within the first few days of illness. Other recommended precautions include wearing well-fitting face masks in crowded indoor spaces, public transport and healthcare facilities, frequent handwashing, covering coughs and sneezes, improving indoor ventilation and avoiding self-medication. For healthcare workers, the Academy called for increased suspicion of COVID-19 among patients presenting with acute respiratory infections, while ensuring that other illnesses, including malaria, influenza, bacterial pneumonia and Lassa fever, are not overlooked. It recommended the use of rapid antigen tests or polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing, with a proportion of positive samples forwarded to designated laboratories for genomic sequencing. Health facilities were also urged to strengthen infection prevention and control measures, separate patients with respiratory symptoms, ensure adequate personal protective equipment, maintain oxygen supplies and check the availability of pulse oximeters and isolation facilities. According to the Academy, clinical management of PJ.2.1 should follow existing national and WHO guidelines for other Omicron sub-lineages. It called on the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare and the NCDC to intensify genomic surveillance, strengthen testing and monitoring at points of entry during the festive travel period. item.title: 2027: APC’ll win three South-East states; Obi will take Abia, Anambra — Bwala
item.description: The Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Policy Communication, Daniel Bwala, has projected that the All Progressives Congress will win three states in the South-East in the 2027 general elections, while conceding that Peter Obi could retain a stronghold in Abia and Anambra. Bwala made the projection during an interview on Channels Television’s Morning Brief on Monday, where he was asked how the ruling party intended to secure victories in the region. He said Obi’s popularity in the two states could make them difficult for the APC to win, but expressed confidence that the party would prevail in the remaining South-East states. “We will struggle in Abia. You see, in Abia and Anambra, Peter has a very convincing presence. Even in these two states, I am assuming that if we lose, we still come second, which is not a bad thing. Apart from these two states, the remainder of the states, we are winning,” Bwala said. The presidential aide, however, stressed that his assessment was a projection rather than a definitive prediction, noting that different political actors could arrive at varying conclusions from available data. He said the party was willing to acknowledge areas where it might face difficulties rather than make sweeping claims about its chances. “Where we think we may not, and I use the word advisedly because none of what I’m saying is cast in stone, right? It is projection, and two people from the same political party can have different projections based on our own interpretation of data,” he said. Bwala added that admitting potential weaknesses was more honest than claiming the APC would win everywhere, noting that his use of the word “struggle” referred specifically to the party’s chances of winning those states. The presidential adviser also expressed confidence in the APC’s overall prospects ahead of the 2027 elections, dismissing the opposition’s preparedness to challenge the ruling party. “I do not think the opposition is ready. Those who understand the political trajectory can see that they are already facing defeat,” he said. item.title: Boat Mishap: Bayelsa Govt To Commission Marine Taskforce In Search Of Missing Persons
item.description: Governor of Bayelsa State, Douye Diri, is set to commission a marine taskforce to intensify the search for victims of a boat mishap that has claimed over 29 lives in the state. The state’s Commissioner for Marine and Blue Economy, Dr. Faith Godwin, who was a guest on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily on Monday, disclosed that the state government will commission a Safety Marine Taskforce this week as part of the effort to ensure compliance with water transportation safety rules across 30 jetties in Bayelsa State. The development followed Friday’s boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, with a death toll of 29 recorded so far and over 50 survivors receiving treatment in hospitals. She noted that the collaborative effort to recover more bodies as the search continues. “Actually, the effort is still ongoing. The state government is represented by the Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy by Alsace State in collaboration with the State Emergency Management Agency, as well as Nigerian Police, Nigerian Navy, Security Agency, Civil Defence and the Community Rescue Team, the Ministry Rescue Team also. The efforts are still ongoing to see how we can recover more bodies.” Bayelsa State Commissioner for Marine and Blue Economy, Dr. Faith Zibs Godwin speaking on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily on Monday, November 22, 2026. On why the operator boat which capsized may have flouted safety rules such as overloading, she said, “According to the Maritime Workers Union, as well as the other team who had been at the unit, they said they had to stay clear because the operator at that time felt they didn’t have the right to talk to him. item.title: Alice Huang Had Contact With China Spy Agency During Nvidia Boss Affair — Reports
item.description: Alice Huang, the alleged spy at the center of the Nvidia scandal, was in touch with an official from China’s top spy agency during an affair with the chip giant’s former chief executive Jensen Huang, the New York Times reported on Sunday. Alice Huang was this month outed as a suspected Chinese spy, accused of having an affair with Jensen Huang while digging up company secrets for Beijing. She was in contact with an officer of China’s Ministry of State Security from the spring of 2025 until the fall of this year, the Times reported, citing people with knowledge of the intelligence. Alice Huang, who is no relation to Jensen, previously led Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based tech group under investigation for allegedly helping Chinese firms gain access to Nvidia chips, possibly in violation of US export controls. Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang arrives ahead of a state banquet for US President Donald Trump and China’s President Xi Jinping at the Great Hall of the People Beijing on May 14, 2026. (Photo by BRENDAN SMIALOWSKI / AFP) According to the Times, Alice Huang’s contacts with the Chinese spy agency correspond to the affair as well as a period when Megaspeed was acquiring large amounts of advanced Nvidia chips. The Times also reported that US intelligence agencies have gathered evidence that Alice Huang’s business partner Kang Wei — who the newspaper said was often introduced as her husband — worked with the same Chinese spy agency. Jensen Huang stepped down as Nvidia’s chief executive earlier this month, following revelations of extramarital affairs, including with Alice Huang. He is to be questioned by US lawmakers on December 1 over national security concerns. The upheaval has battered shares of Nvidia which is at the center of an AI boom that has helped propel markets to record highs and boosted economic growth around the globe. item.title: Abia Police condemn officers over pregnant woman’s hospital ordeal
item.description: By Steve Oko The Abia State Police Command has condemned the conduct of some of its personnel who allegedly stopped a man conveying his pregnant wife to hospital over the absence of a displayed vehicle number plate. The incident, captured in a viral video that has generated reactions on social media, involved officers attached to the Surveillance Patrol and Guard Team of Ubakala Divisional Police Station. The man was reportedly taking his pregnant wife to hospital after she began experiencing labour contractions when he encountered the officers, who allegedly insisted on taking him to the police station for driving without a displayed registration number plate. Reacting to the incident, the Police Command said it had identified the officers involved and commenced an investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the encounter and determine their level of responsibility. In a statement issued by the Police Public Relations Officer, Maureen Chinaka, the Command acknowledged that the man was driving without a displayed number plate, contrary to road traffic regulations. It explained that vehicle identification was important, particularly in view of prevailing security challenges, including vehicle theft and the use of unidentified vehicles for criminal activities. The Command, however, said enforcement of traffic regulations should be guided by sound judgment and consideration for human welfare, especially in emergency situations. On the claim that the man’s wife was in labour, the police said preliminary information indicated that she was fine and had not given birth as of the time of the statement. It added that no medical evidence had been presented to substantiate the claim that she was about to deliver. Despite this, the Command expressed displeasure over what it described as the officers’ apparent failure to demonstrate sufficient empathy towards the pregnant woman. The outgoing Commissioner of Police, AIG Wilfred Olutokunbo Afolabi, reiterated that the police had a statutory responsibility not only to prevent and detect crime and maintain law and order but also to protect lives, uphold citizens’ rights and assist people in distress. He stressed that police duties must be discharged with professionalism, empathy, restraint and respect for human dignity. According to him, although the Command would continue to enforce the law, such responsibilities must be carried out with humanity and consideration for prevailing circumstances. The Command assured members of the public that the investigation would be thorough and that appropriate disciplinary measures would be taken if misconduct was established. item.title: Troops clear suspected IPOB/ESN camp, neutralise IEDs in Imo
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of the Nigerian Army, working alongside other security agencies, have cleared additional sections of a suspected Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) and Eastern Security Network (ESN) camp in Imo State, uncovering and neutralising improvised explosive devices (IEDs). The operation, conducted on November 21 around Awomama in Oru East Local Government Area, was part of ongoing security offensives launched on November 16 and 17, according to the Army. The joint operation involved troops of the 34 Artillery Brigade and personnel of the Nigerian Navy, Nigerian Air Force, Nigeria Police Force, Department of State Services (DSS) and Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC). Security sources said the joint team advanced into the Tango 2 and Tango 3 sections of the suspected camp at about 6:30 a.m., where they discovered that the locations had been heavily fortified with explosives. With the support of Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) personnel, the troops located and successfully neutralised the improvised explosive devices. The operation also led to the recovery of two battery components suspected to have been used to trigger the explosives. The clearance operation is part of sustained efforts by security agencies to dismantle suspected criminal hideouts and prevent attacks in the area. item.title: PANDEF mourns Bayelsa boat accident victims, urges coastal roads
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Pan Niger Delta Forum (PANDEF) has mourned victims of the boat accident around Oweikorogha Community in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, which reportedly claimed several lives, including youths and children. The socio-political organisation also renewed its call on the Federal Government and governments of oil-producing states to prioritise the construction of roads and bridges to connect isolated coastal communities and reduce their dependence on water transportation. PANDEF, in a statement signed by its National Chairman, Ambassador Godknows Igali, said it received the news of the accident, which occurred on Friday, November 20, 2026, with shock and sadness. The organisation described the incident as heartbreaking and commiserated with the affected families, the Bayelsa State Government, residents of Southern Ijaw and the affected communities. It said the tragedy reinforced its longstanding position that inadequate road infrastructure had left many coastal communities with limited transportation options, making water travel a necessity for their residents. According to PANDEF, the Federal Government should, as an interim measure, support state governments in acquiring adequate seaworthy vessels to meet the transportation needs of coastal communities. The organisation also called on emergency relief agencies, security agencies and regulatory authorities to work with the Bayelsa State Government to provide assistance to survivors and bereaved families. It urged the relevant authorities to strengthen enforcement of water transportation safety regulations, including compliance with passenger safety protocols, the use of appropriate safety equipment and the operation of vessels that meet prescribed seaworthiness standards. PANDEF said measures must be taken to prevent a recurrence of such tragedies, stressing the need for improved transportation infrastructure and stricter safety standards across the coastal areas. The statement read in part: “While mourning this tragic loss, PANDEF calls on the relevant emergency relief agencies, security agencies and regulatory authorities to work closely with the Bayelsa State Government to ensure that all necessary measures are taken to assuage the impact on survivors and bereaved families. “More importantly, [they should] take all necessary measures to prevent a recurrence of such tragedies.” The organisation expressed solidarity with the victims’ families and the people of Bayelsa State, praying for the repose of the souls of the deceased and comfort for those affected by the tragedy. item.title: Alice Huang had contact with China spy agency during Nvidia boss affair – Report
item.description: Alice Huang, the alleged spy at the center of the Nvidia scandal, was in touch with an official from China’s top spy agency during an affair with the chip giant’s former chief executive Jensen Huang, the New York Times reported on Sunday. Alice Huang was this month outed as a suspected Chinese spy, accused of having an affair with Jensen Huang while digging up company secrets for Beijing. She was in contact with an officer of China’s Ministry of State Security from the spring of 2025 until the fall of this year, the Times reported, citing people with knowledge of the intelligence. Alice Huang, who is no relation to Jensen, previously led Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based tech group under investigation for allegedly helping Chinese firms gain access to Nvidia chips, possibly in violation of US export controls. According to the Times, Alice Huang’s contacts with the Chinese spy agency correspond to the affair as well as a period when Megaspeed was acquiring large amounts of advanced Nvidia chips. The Times also reported that US intelligence agencies have gathered evidence that Alice Huang’s business partner Kang Wei — who the newspaper said was often introduced as her husband — worked with the same Chinese spy agency. Jensen Huang stepped down as Nvidia’s chief executive earlier this month, following revelations of extramarital affairs, including with Alice Huang. He is to be questioned by US lawmakers on December 1 over national security concerns. The upheaval has battered shares of Nvidia which is at the center of an AI boom that has helped propel markets to record highs and boosted economic growth around the globe. item.title: Senegal to know fate of AFCON title appeal Tuesday – CAS
item.description: The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) announced that a verdict on Senegal’s appeal of the decision to strip them of the Africa Cup of Nations title in favour of Morocco will come on Tuesday. CAS’s ruling comes after a hearing of the case, over a chaotic AFCON final in January, which took place behind closed doors at its headquarters in Lausanne on October 8. “The parties have been notified that the CAS decision will be rendered Tuesday 24 November 2026 in the course of the afternoon (GMT),” CAS said in a short statement on Monday. At the January 18 final in Rabat, Senegal won 1-0 thanks to Pape Gueye’s extra-time goal, but the occasion was marred near the end of normal time when many Senegal players walked off the pitch in protest at the decision to award Morocco a penalty with the match still goalless. Some Senegalese supporters also attempted a pitch invasion, and the game was held up for almost 20 minutes before the Senegal players returned. In March, the Confederation of African Football (CAF) overturned that result, awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory, and the title. In response, the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) denounced the ruling as the “most blatant administrative robbery in the history of our sport”. The Senegal team even paraded the trophy to their supporters in Paris at the end of March. The post Senegal to know fate of AFCON title appeal Tuesday – CAS appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.description: A fire outbreak at Kano Fish Market along Zaria Road has destroyed more than 100 shops, leaving traders counting losses estimated to run into billions of naira. The fire reportedly broke out at about 9:00 p.m. on Sunday, near Kano Line Motor Park, spreading across sections of the market and destroying shops, containers and goods. Reports indicate that approximately 150 shops and 200 containers were affected by the inferno, with some traders reportedly losing goods valued at millions of naira. item.title: UK Digging New Reservoirs To Fight Persistent Droughts
item.description: Britain has long had a reputation for rain. But as it adapts to a warmer, drier climate, the UK is racing to complete a huge new reservoir, its first in over three decades. Bulldozers have been digging up the ground for the vast £800-million ($1 billion) Havant Thicket project near the southern coastal port of Portsmouth. Like much of Europe, Britain endured record-breaking heat this summer and, despite the return of rains as the country moves into winter, parts are still grappling with drought conditions. “We’ve got increasing problems with our water security in the UK,” climate scientist Hannah Cloke from Reading University told AFP. “We need to really think about how we’re storing that water because this problem is only going to get worse.” Scientists have warned extreme weather events are likely to become more frequent and more intense as the global climate changes. Workers carry out construction work at the site of the new Havant Thicket Reservoir in Hampshire, southern England, on November 5, 2026. Photo by CARLOS JASSO / AFP By mid-November, almost all of England remained in drought, with some areas classified as suffering severe drought, according to the Environment Agency. Potentially exacerbating matters, existing reservoirs were only 60 percent full, 19 percentage points below the seasonal average. For policymakers, the situation poses a longer-term challenge as the thirst for water increases with a rising population and the growth of heavy water-using industries such as data centres. Under England’s National Framework for Water Resources published in 2025, the country could face a daily water supply shortfall of five billion litres (1.3 billion gallons) by 2055, with resources under pressure. At the sprawling Havant Thicket site, Portsmouth Water chief executive Bob Taylor said the industry was waking up to the scale of the challenge after successive droughts and hot summers. Workers carry out construction work at the site of the new Havant Thicket Reservoir in Hampshire, southern England, on November 5, 2026. Photo by CARLOS JASSO / AFP The issue, he stressed, was not necessarily how much rain falls over the course of a year, but when it falls. Winters are becoming wetter, while summers are increasingly dry. “Without reservoirs you can’t store that intense rainfall and put it somewhere where it can be used at another time,” Taylor said. The new reservoir will eventually hold up to 8.7 billion litres of water, helping secure supplies for hundreds of thousands of people. Fed in part by winter surpluses from a major spring already tapped by Portsmouth Water, it has become one of the flagship projects in a broader shift in Britain’s water strategy. The government has approved the construction of nine major reservoirs by 2050, and last year relaxed planning rules to speed up projects after decades of under-investment in water infrastructure. Together, the future reservoirs could deliver an additional 670 million litres of water per day. ‘

According to Taylor, it is expected to become operational by 2032 or 2033. Combined with a planned wastewater recycling plant being developed by Southern Water which still needs approval, it is expected to supply up to 111 million litres a day. The recycling facility has, however, sparked strong local opposition. The woman, identified as Mirka and known on Instagram by the handle @beduinqa, posted the video after completing a 30-day tour of different parts of Nigeria.
